limitations: Derived by an REA+ composed workflow.
After retirement, reopen the target to resolve its saved generation; an old profile cannot silently restart from changed state. Publisher locks are not reclaimed automatically after owner crashes.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
External functions and functions without an analyzable body return null; other decompiler failures remain explicit.
External functions and local thunks are distinct; procedure metadata identifies both and preserves a thunk target when Ghidra resolves one.
Ghidra auto-analysis state: analysis_complete=true; analysis_timed_out=false.

Owned Ghidra checkpoints save the initial Program and every acknowledged metadata edit. Restores use a verified private copy without rerunning auto-analysis, and preserve the original timeout and seed identity. Original executable bytes are never written.
Pseudocode is Ghidra decompiler output, not original source and not text-equivalent to Hopper output.

The default profile requires Ghidra to report default auto-analysis complete; an explicitly bounded profile can admit a stable partial Program after its configured deadline. Every observation reports the measured analysis outcome.
macOS sessions require a matching executable Ghidra native decompiler; REA+ checks for it but does not build native components or change Gatekeeper quarantine state.
unknowns: The batch covers its explicit ordered selectors only; unavailable pseudocode and unknown procedure identity remain unresolved.
